page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a performance profile characterized by moderate single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory throughput. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the average tier, supported by single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core execution is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers registering at 30.99 GB/sec and write operations at 25.51 GB/sec, both of which rank in the lower tier.

The primary tradeoff of this instance lies in its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and the lack of local storage, which requires external block storage for data persistence. While the dedicated 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon cores offer stable single-threaded execution, the weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth limit its utility for heavy parallel processing or memory-intensive databases. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources with low memory footprints, such as lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, or small-scale text processing tasks.

Configured with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and no local storage, it relies on external network storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. This resource profile presents a clear tradeoff: while dedicated high-frequency cores support stable single-threaded tasks, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and constrained multi-core scaling limit its effectiveness for parallel processing. The instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and small-scale text processing workloads where high memory capacity is not required.
